title: VPC Autosafeguard: offline simulation + policy-driven safe apply for batching & cache tuning
creator: Arjun Patel
description: Goal: build an Autosafeguard subsystem for Private/VPC/on-prem deployments that performs offline simulation of batching and KV/prefix-caching recommendations, enforces organization policies, and produces auditable safe-apply/rollback plans. This ticket covers the orchestration, policy driver, offline verification harness, and the initial control-plane integration for staged apply in VPC/private mode where live probing is restricted. The system must default to conservative configs, detect risky regressions (latency and unit-cost), and produce a reversible, auditable change set for operator approval or automated safe rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Offline sim can run against a captured 24h request sample and produce per-route recommendations for batch_size, kv_cache_ttl, and prefix_cache_enabled
Policy engine evaluates every recommendation against org rules and emits allow/warn/deny with rule names and rationale
Plan generator produces a staged apply with: dry-run diff, canary subset (3 nodes / 1% traffic equivalent), rollback steps, and estimated unit-cost delta
Apply must be rejectable automatically if simulated p95 latency increases by >5% or unit token cost increases by >4% for any route marked "critical"
Audit log contains full before/after configs, metric deltas, simulation artifacts, and decision records (who/what/when)
Manual apply path in Private control plane displays human-friendly risk summary and single-click approval that records SSO identity
tasks: Design offline simulation schema and lightweight capture adapter for VPC (proto: sim-capture-v1)
Implement policy driver with expressive rule language (baseline: token-cost threshold, latency threshold, route whitelists, model-variant constraints)
Build plan generator that translates recommendations into ordered, reversible steps and a canary subset definition
Integrate simulator with existing perf harness to compute p50/p95/p99 and token-unit cost delta per route
Add audit log writer and signed plan artifact stored in customer namespace with retention metadata
Console UI: Plan review page for Private customers (prototype only, PM will wire final)
E2E test harness to run sim -> policy -> plan -> apply on a private staging cluster (no external network egress)
risks: Simulator divergence: captured workload may not match production distribution leading to false negatives/positives
Policy expressiveness: building too many ad-hoc rules increases maintenance cost; need a small, testable core
Approval latency: requiring manual approval for many small recs could negate cost savings
Data sensitivity: captured traces include token prefixes or prompts; must honor redaction/KMS policies
Rollback complexity: some cache changes require warm-up; rollback must account for transient cost/latency artifacts
rollout_plan: MVP: internal dogfood in on-prem staging cluster (team-only) for two weeks
Phase 1: invite-only beta for 3 existing Private customers with signed NDA; run offline sim only (no auto-apply)
Phase 2: staged apply enabled for 'non-critical' routes with automated canary and automated rollback triggers
Phase 3: broader GA with policy template catalog and prebuilt conservative defaults for regulated customers
test_plan: Unit tests for policy driver rule evaluation (>= 95% branch coverage)
Synthetic workload regression tests: run sim against golden traces and assert no >5% regression on p95 and cost <= +3%
Chaos: simulate node restarts during staged apply to validate rollback idempotency
Privacy test: ensure capture adapter strips/derives PII and that artifacts are encrypted at rest with KMS keys
metrics: Simulation accuracy (post-apply measured delta vs predicted delta) target: <= 10% error
Number of auto-blocked recommendations due to policy (weekly)
Percentage of safe-auto-applies that required rollback within 72h
Customer-reported incidents caused by optimization changes (target: zero for beta)
